posts.author: thycore
posts.post_subject: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.content_md:
Hi there,

An old (and closed) topic on the forum : [https://holowiki.org/forum/viewtopic.ph ... cb6#p57579](https://holowiki.org/forum/viewtopic.php?f=30&t=7304&hilit=blackening#p57579)

Refers as a technique from Jeff Blyth to use Sodium Borohydride (Tétrahydruroborate de sodium in french) to blackens the rear part of the emulsion after it's been developed, bleached and **dryied**. I can't wait to test this technique, I ordered some NaBH4 on eBay.

The formula provided for this blackening bath is as follows :

650ml methanol

350ml dionized water 

0.5g sodium borohydride

Any idea if Isopropyl alcool (IPA) can be used instead of Methanol ? (I have like tons of this at home..)

posts.topic_title: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.author: BobH
posts.post_subject: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.content_md: What difficulties have you had with paint? A solution may be to seal the hologram with epoxy or RTV (like Ron & Bernadette Olson use), and a piece of glass. Then paint the back. Use a piece of smoked or black glass and you may not need to paint.

posts.topic_title: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.author: soda
posts.post_subject: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.content_md: The best way how to handle the holofilm250 I found use few drops of LOCA uv glue (cheap on ebay for cell phone repair) to sandwich it to glass and press the sandwich firmly, then irradiate it by the UV lamp (or direct sun). Then the hologram can be used as master from the other side, or simply paint the back glass to black. An acrylate based black spray also can be applied directly to the emulsion side.

posts.content_md: What exactly does UV on this film ? Do you use it on freshly developed / bleached film ? Is it acting like a « fixer » ?

posts.topic_title: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.author: soda
posts.post_subject: Blackening the emulsion for reflexion holograms
posts.content_md:
The UV cures the LOCA glue. Complete sequence is: Pre-swell the film to get blue shift and replay in green. I use alcohol with small amount of water. The amount of the water control the blue shift. Simply drop few drops on glass and lay the film on it, add another drops and add another glass. Wait few minutes and the sandwich is ready to be exposed by pulsed ruby. For CW is better to use TEA. You can skip this step if you use chrome bleach or you want to preserve original color. After exposition I develop it roughly 2min in SM6 (for CW work CW-C2 should be better) and bleached it in Brilland bleach. After slow and complete drying I drop small amount of LOCA to clean glass, lay on it the hologram and press it by another glass. Then expose it to UV to cure the LOCA glue - resulting with permanently attached hologram to glass. The LOCA glue have simillar index of ref. as glass, the interface between disappears.

See the result - H2 copy of this way processed pulsed ruby master, dandelion in my dirty fingers
